big_idea: We use the data to make PREDICTIONS. If 1 tap fills 1 bucket, then 5 taps fill 5 buckets.
learning_intention: We are learning to use data to predict an outcome.
student_learning_goal: I can use data to predict an outcome.
success_criteria: I can use a 1-to-1 rule (1 tap = 1 bucket) to predict.
I can predict for 5, 10, even 20 trees.
I can explain how I made my prediction.
lesson_specific_materials: Per-pair set of paper trees and paper buckets
Lesson 3 prediction tracker — provided in assessment_suite stage

minds_on.hook: If 1 tree fills 1 bucket of sap, how many buckets for 5 trees? 10 trees?
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Sap Sam in hand. 'Friends — yesterday we collected DATA. Today we use the data to PREDICT.'

'Sap Sam knows: 1 tree fills 1 bucket. That's our DATA. Now predict — how many buckets for 5 trees?' Children: '5!' 'Right. We use the rule (1 tree = 1 bucket) to predict.'

Write on the chart: '5 trees × 1 bucket each = 5 buckets.'

'Predict for 10 trees. 10 buckets. For 20? 20 buckets. The rule scales.'

Now harder. 'What if some trees give MORE? Big trees give 2 buckets. Small trees give 1.' Build with paper: 5 big trees + 5 small trees. Predict: 5×2 + 5×1 = 10 + 5 = 15 buckets.

'Predicting helps us plan. Sap Sam knows how many buckets to bring to the bush.'

steps.instruction: Whole group: predict for 4 more scenarios. (a) 8 trees, 1 bucket each. (b) 6 trees, 2 buckets each. (c) 10 trees, half big half small. (d) 15 trees, 1 bucket each.
steps.teacher_prompt: Say to students: 'Use the rule. Predict the buckets.'

steps.instruction: Send pairs to three stations (~7 min each). Station A: Tree-to-Bucket — pair predicts buckets for 5, 10, 15 trees with 1-bucket-each rule. Station B: Mixed Sizes — pair predicts for groups of big and small trees. Station C: Real-Life Predict — pair counts something then predicts (e.g., 'I have 5 friends. If each gets 2 stickers, how many stickers?').
steps.teacher_prompt: Say to students: 'Three stations, 7 minutes each.'

steps.instruction: Stretch challenge at Station C: include problems where predictions might be wrong (variability — some trees give MORE than 1 bucket, some give LESS).
steps.teacher_prompt: Say to pairs: 'Sometimes predictions need a range, not a single number.'

steps.instruction: Discuss the rule. 'A model is a RULE that says how things relate. 1 tree = 1 bucket is a rule. Different rules give different predictions.'
Circulate to record formative evidence on the prediction tracker.
steps.teacher_prompt: Stop at each pair. Ask 'What's your rule? What's your prediction?' Mark the tracker.

differentiation.for_emerging: Stay at Station A. Use only 1-bucket-each rule.
differentiation.for_extending: Stretch at Station B: predict for 50 trees with mixed sizes.
differentiation.for_ell_or_iep: Provide picture-supported tree-bucket cards. Sentence frame: 'For ___ trees, I predict ___ buckets.'
differentiation.for_movement_learners: Walk-and-count: pretend each step is a tree, each foot's bucket prediction is the count.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Three signals: applies a rule to predict; predicts for varying counts; explains the rule.
formative_check.how_to_record: Tick the prediction tracker per child.

discussion_prompts: How did you make your prediction?
Can a rule be wrong sometimes?
What's one prediction you made today?
consolidation.exit_routine: Each child writes ONE prediction on a sticky note: 'For ___, I predict ___.' Notes go on the chart.

assessment_in_this_lesson.rationale: Lesson 3 captures the PREDICT step of the modelling cycle.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child predicts a single number when reality has variability — repairing the over-confident prediction error
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
The most common Grade-1 trap on prediction is the over-confident error: the child predicts exactly 5 buckets for 5 trees without considering that some trees might give more or less. They miss that real-life predictions often need a RANGE.

The walkthrough covers the precise moment when a child predicts 5 buckets and is surprised when reality gives 4.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Pair is at Station C. The child predicts 5 buckets for 5 trees. Reality: 4 buckets (one tree was dry).
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
'Your prediction was 5. Reality was 4. What happened?' The child shrugs. 'Sometimes real life is DIFFERENT from our rules. Trees aren't all identical.'

'Sap Sam says — predict a RANGE. Maybe 4-6 buckets. Then your prediction includes uncertainty.'

Long-term recovery: every prediction includes a 'maybe range'.
common_misconceptions: Predictions are always exact. (Repair: real life has variability.)
Rules always work. (Repair: rules are estimates.)
If reality differs from prediction, the prediction was 'wrong'. (Repair: predictions are estimates — close is good.)

parts_outline.task: Use the rule '1 tree = 1 bucket' to predict for 4 different tree counts.
Use a different rule (e.g., 1 tree = 2 buckets) and predict.
Pick a real-life rule from your day. Predict for one situation.
